concepts.description: Networks in which information flows in one direction from input through hidden layers to output, forming the basic architecture covered in the lecture.
concepts.name: Feedforward Neural Networks

concepts.description: An application of the chain rule that propagates error gradients backward through the network layer by layer to update weights.
concepts.name: Backpropagation

concepts.description: Nonlinear functions such as ReLU, sigmoid, and tanh applied to neuron outputs so the network can model nonlinear relationships.
concepts.name: Activation Functions

concepts.description: An optimization method that updates weights using gradients estimated from mini-batches of training data rather than the full dataset.
concepts.name: Stochastic Gradient Descent

concepts.description: A loss function paired with softmax outputs that measures the divergence between predicted class probabilities and true labels for classification.
concepts.name: Cross-Entropy Loss

concepts.description: An output layer function that converts raw scores into a probability distribution over classes for classification tasks.
concepts.name: Softmax Output

concepts.description: Methods such as L2 weight decay and dropout that reduce overfitting by constraining model complexity or randomly deactivating units during training.
concepts.name: Regularization Techniques

concepts.description: Training problems in deep networks where gradients shrink or grow exponentially across layers, hindering effective learning.
concepts.name: Vanishing and Exploding Gradients

concepts.description: A technique that normalizes layer inputs over each mini-batch, which stabilizes and speeds up optimization.
concepts.name: Batch Normalization
